title: When Daddy Fell into the Pond
subject: English
chapter: 7. Poem: When Daddy Fell into the Pond
description: Grammar-focused practice for the chapter: kinds of nouns (proper, common, countable, uncountable, collective, concrete, abstract) and articles (a, an, the, zero article), with poem comprehension, vocabulary, and figures of speech from 'Daddy Fell into the Pond' by Alfred Noyes.

questions.question: What is a noun?
options: A naming word for a person, place, animal, or thing
A word that describes a noun
A word that joins two sentences
questions.explanation: A noun is a naming word — it names a person, place, animal, or thing.

questions.question: Which of these is a PROPER noun?
questions.explanation: 'Dublin' is the name of a specific place, so it is a proper noun. Proper nouns always begin with a capital letter.

questions.question: Which of these is a COMMON noun?
questions.explanation: 'teacher' is a general name for a person, so it is a common noun. The others name specific people, places, or days.

questions.question: A proper noun always begins with a capital letter.
questions.explanation: Proper nouns name specific people, places, or things and always begin with a capital letter, like 'Timothy' or 'Ireland'.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Timothy danced with joy', which word is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: 'Timothy' is the name of a specific person, making it a proper noun.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a proper noun correctly with a capital letter?
options: We visited a Country last summer.
We visited the city Dublin without a capital.
questions.explanation: 'Ireland' is a proper noun naming a specific country, so it must begin with a capital letter.

questions.question: Select ALL the proper nouns.
questions.explanation: 'Dublin' and 'Timothy' name specific places and people. 'boy' and 'pond' are general (common) nouns.

questions.question: Select ALL the common nouns.
questions.explanation: 'camera', 'gardener', and 'duck' are general names, so they are common nouns. 'Ireland' names a specific place, so it is a proper noun.

questions.question: Which word names a general place, making it a common noun?
questions.explanation: 'market' is a general name for a place, so it is a common noun. The others name specific places.

questions.question: The word 'gardener' is a common noun.
questions.explanation: 'gardener' is a general name for a person who works in a garden, so it is a common noun.

questions.question: In 'My friend Sara lives in a big city', which word is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: 'Sara' is the name of a specific person, so it is a proper noun. 'friend' and 'city' are common nouns, and 'big' is an adjective.

questions.question: Which sentence has a proper noun that is INCORRECTLY written without a capital letter?
options: We saw the taj mahal in agra.
We saw the Taj Mahal in Agra.
We saw a monument in a town.
questions.explanation: 'taj mahal' and 'agra' are proper nouns and should be capitalised as 'Taj Mahal' and 'Agra'.

questions.question: Which of these is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: 'Monday' is the name of a specific day, so it is a proper noun. The others are common nouns.

questions.question: Which pair correctly shows a common noun and its matching proper noun?
questions.explanation: 'country' is the common (general) noun and 'India' is the proper (specific) noun that names one particular country.

questions.question: The word 'Sunday' is a common noun because it is a day of the week.
questions.explanation: 'Sunday' is a proper noun — it names a specific day and always begins with a capital letter.

questions.question: Which word is a common noun in 'The dog ran across the park'?
questions.explanation: 'dog' is a general name for an animal, so it is a common noun. ('park' is also a common noun.)

questions.question: Rehan read a story in the library. Which words are the common nouns?
questions.explanation: 'story' and 'library' are general names, so they are common nouns. 'Rehan' is a proper noun, and 'read' is a verb.

questions.question: Proper nouns name ____, while common nouns name ____.
options: specific people or places; general people or things
questions.explanation: Proper nouns name specific people, places, or things (with a capital letter), while common nouns are general names.

questions.question: The word 'pond' in the poem is a common noun.
questions.explanation: 'pond' is a general name for a body of water, so it is a common noun.

questions.question: Which sentence contains BOTH a proper noun and a common noun?
questions.explanation: 'Sara' is a proper noun (specific person) and 'cat' is a common noun (general animal), so this sentence has both.

questions.question: Which of these should always start with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: Proper nouns — names of specific people and places — always start with a capital letter.

questions.question: In 'Daddy fell into the pond', which best describes the word 'Daddy' as used here?
options: It is used as a proper noun, naming one specific person
questions.explanation: In the poem, 'Daddy' is used as a name for one specific person, so it acts as a proper noun and is capitalised.

questions.question: Select ALL the words that should be written with a capital letter as proper nouns.
questions.explanation: 'timothy' (Timothy) and 'monday' (Monday) are proper nouns and need capital letters. 'camera' and 'gardener' are common nouns.

questions.question: Which word is the proper noun in 'People speak Japanese in Japan'?
questions.explanation: 'Japan' is a specific country, making it a proper noun. ('Japanese' is also a proper noun as a language name.)

questions.question: What is a countable noun?
options: A noun we can count and make plural, like 'books'
A noun we cannot count, like 'water'
A noun that names a feeling
A noun that names a group
questions.explanation: Countable nouns can be counted and have singular and plural forms, like 'one book, two books'.

questions.question: Which of these is an UNCOUNTABLE noun?
questions.explanation: 'milk' cannot be counted directly (we don't say 'two milks'), so it is uncountable. The others can be counted.

questions.question: Which of these is a COUNTABLE noun?
questions.explanation: 'pencil' can be counted (one pencil, two pencils), so it is countable. The others are uncountable.

questions.question: Countable nouns can be made plural, like 'one cat, two cats'.
questions.explanation: Countable nouns have both singular and plural forms, so we can say 'one cat, two cats'.

questions.question: The word 'water' is a countable noun.
questions.explanation: 'water' is uncountable — we cannot say 'two waters'. We measure it instead, like 'a glass of water'.

questions.question: Select ALL the COUNTABLE nouns.
questions.explanation: 'book', 'chair', and 'star' can be counted. 'rice' is usually uncountable — we measure it, not count each grain.

questions.question: Select ALL the UNCOUNTABLE nouns.
questions.explanation: 'sugar', 'milk', and 'sand' are uncountable — we measure them. 'pencil' can be counted.

questions.question: Which phrase correctly measures an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: Uncountable nouns are measured using words like 'a glass of', so 'a glass of water' is correct.

questions.question: Which sentence uses an uncountable noun correctly?
options: I need some information about the trip.
I need some informations about the trip.
questions.explanation: 'information' is uncountable, so it has no plural form. We say 'some information', not 'informations'.

questions.question: How do we usually talk about the amount of an uncountable noun?
options: By using measuring words like 'a cup of' or 'a piece of'
questions.explanation: Because uncountable nouns can't be counted directly, we use measuring words like 'a cup of tea' or 'a piece of bread'.

questions.question: Which of these can be BOTH counted and made plural?
questions.explanation: 'oranges' is countable and plural (one orange, two oranges). Honey, butter, and flour are uncountable.

questions.question: The word 'furniture' is a countable noun, so we can say 'two furnitures'.
questions.explanation: 'furniture' is uncountable. We say 'two pieces of furniture', not 'two furnitures'.

questions.question: Which word is countable?
questions.explanation: 'egg' can be counted (one egg, two eggs), so it is countable. The others are uncountable.

questions.question: 'I bought three ____ of chocolate.' Which word best fills the blank?
questions.explanation: We measure chocolate with a counting word like 'bars', so 'three bars of chocolate' is correct.

questions.question: Which noun below would you measure rather than count?
questions.explanation: 'salt' is uncountable and is measured (a pinch of salt). Spoon, plate, and bowl can be counted.

questions.question: Select ALL the sentences that use countable/uncountable nouns correctly.
options: She drank a glass of milk.
questions.explanation: 'a glass of milk' and 'two apples' are correct. 'rices' and 'breads' are wrong because rice and bread are uncountable.

questions.question: What is a collective noun?
options: A word that names a group of people, animals, or things
A word that names one person
A word that describes a noun
questions.explanation: A collective noun names a whole group as one unit, like 'a team' or 'a herd'.

questions.question: Which of these is a collective noun?
questions.explanation: 'team' names a group of players, so it is a collective noun.

questions.question: Which collective noun is used for a group of students?
questions.explanation: 'class' is the collective noun for a group of students.

questions.question: Which collective noun goes with 'sheep'?
questions.explanation: A group of sheep is called 'a flock of sheep'.

questions.question: Which collective noun goes with 'wolves'?
questions.explanation: A group of wolves is called 'a pack of wolves'.

questions.question: Which collective noun goes with 'bees'?
questions.explanation: A group of bees is called 'a swarm of bees'.

questions.question: Which collective noun goes with 'flowers'?
questions.explanation: A group of flowers is called 'a bunch of flowers' (or 'a bouquet of flowers').

questions.question: A collective noun names a whole group as a single unit.
questions.explanation: That is exactly what a collective noun does — it names a group, like 'a team' or 'a class', as one unit.

questions.question: In 'The team of players celebrated their victory', which word is the collective noun?
questions.explanation: 'team' names the group of players, so it is the collective noun.

questions.question: Which collective noun goes with 'ships'?
questions.explanation: A group of ships is called 'a fleet of ships'.

questions.question: Which collective noun goes with 'cows'?
questions.explanation: A group of cows is called 'a herd of cows'.

questions.question: Select ALL the collective nouns.
questions.explanation: 'army' and 'bunch' name groups, so they are collective nouns. 'soldier' and 'flower' name single things.

questions.question: A group of birds is called a ____.
questions.explanation: A group of birds is called a 'flock'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a collective noun?
options: A bunch of grapes is on the table.
The grape is on the table.
questions.explanation: 'bunch' is a collective noun naming a group of grapes, so the first sentence uses one.

questions.question: Which collective noun goes with 'stars'?
questions.explanation: A group of stars is called 'a cluster of stars' (or a constellation).

questions.question: The word 'family' is a collective noun.
questions.explanation: 'family' names a group of related people as one unit, so it is a collective noun.

questions.question: Which of these names a group of soldiers?
questions.explanation: A group of soldiers is called an 'army'.

questions.question: 'A ____ of wolves hunted together in the forest.' Which collective noun fits best?
questions.explanation: The correct collective noun for wolves is 'pack', so 'a pack of wolves' fits best.

questions.question: Which word tells us a collective noun is present in 'a herd of elephants'?
questions.explanation: 'herd' is the collective noun that names the group of elephants.

questions.question: A 'crowd' is a collective noun because it names a group of people.
questions.explanation: 'crowd' names a group of people gathered together, so it is a collective noun.

questions.question: What is a concrete noun?
options: A noun for something we can see, touch, hear, smell, or taste
A noun for a feeling or idea
A noun that names a group
questions.explanation: A concrete noun names something we can experience with our senses, like 'table' or 'flower'.

questions.question: What is an abstract noun?
options: A noun for a feeling, idea, or quality we cannot touch
A noun we can see and touch
A noun that names a place
A noun that names an animal
questions.explanation: An abstract noun names something we cannot see or touch, like 'honesty', 'joy', or 'friendship'.

questions.question: Which of these is an ABSTRACT noun?
questions.explanation: 'friendship' is a feeling/idea we cannot touch, so it is an abstract noun.

questions.question: Which of these is a CONCRETE noun?
questions.explanation: 'camera' can be seen and touched, so it is a concrete noun. The others are abstract.

questions.question: The word 'honesty' is an abstract noun.
questions.explanation: 'honesty' names a quality we cannot see or touch, so it is an abstract noun.

questions.question: The word 'book' is a concrete noun.
questions.explanation: 'book' is something we can see and touch, so it is a concrete noun.

questions.question: In 'The teacher praised the class for their honesty', which word is the abstract noun?
questions.explanation: 'honesty' is a quality that cannot be touched, so it is the abstract noun. 'class' is collective and 'teacher' is common.

questions.question: In 'The team celebrated their victory', which word is the abstract noun?
questions.explanation: 'victory' is an idea/feeling of winning that cannot be touched, so it is the abstract noun.

questions.question: Select ALL the ABSTRACT nouns.
questions.explanation: 'joy' and 'courage' are feelings/qualities, so they are abstract. 'table' and 'pencil' can be touched, so they are concrete.

questions.question: Select ALL the CONCRETE nouns.
questions.explanation: 'dog' and 'flower' can be seen and touched, so they are concrete. 'kindness' and 'beauty' are abstract.

questions.question: Which sentence contains an abstract noun?
options: The book is on the shelf.
questions.explanation: 'bravery' is a quality we cannot touch, so it is an abstract noun. The other sentences use only concrete nouns.

questions.question: Which word names a feeling and is therefore abstract?
questions.explanation: 'delight' is a feeling of joy that cannot be touched, so it is an abstract noun.

questions.question: In the poem, 'Timothy danced for sheer delight.' Which word is an abstract noun?
questions.explanation: 'delight' is a feeling and cannot be touched, so it is an abstract noun. 'Timothy' is proper and 'danced' is a verb.

questions.question: The word 'library' is an abstract noun because it holds knowledge.
questions.explanation: 'library' is a concrete noun — it is a place we can see and visit, even though it holds books and knowledge.

questions.question: Which of these is an abstract noun?
questions.explanation: 'freedom' is an idea we cannot touch, so it is abstract. The others are concrete.

questions.question: Which of these is a concrete noun?
questions.explanation: 'mountain' can be seen and touched, so it is concrete. Happiness, anger, and love are abstract.

questions.question: Select ALL the abstract nouns from the list.
questions.explanation: 'kindness' and 'hope' are qualities/feelings, so they are abstract. 'spoon' and 'window' are concrete.

questions.question: Which noun is abstract in 'The children showed great patience while waiting'?
questions.explanation: 'patience' is a quality that cannot be touched, so it is abstract. 'children' is concrete and 'great' is an adjective.

questions.question: We can experience concrete nouns with our five senses.
questions.explanation: Concrete nouns can be seen, touched, heard, smelled, or tasted — they are experienced with our senses.

questions.question: Which group contains ONLY abstract nouns?
questions.explanation: 'love', 'fear', and 'honesty' are all feelings or qualities that cannot be touched, so they are all abstract nouns.

questions.question: In 'Rehan read a story about friendship in the library', how many nouns are there?
questions.explanation: The nouns are Rehan (proper), story (common), friendship (abstract), and library (common/concrete) — four in total.

questions.question: In 'My brother bought a box of chocolates from the market', which word is a collective-style container noun?
questions.explanation: 'box' names a container holding a group of chocolates. 'brother' and 'market' are common nouns, and 'chocolates' are concrete.

questions.question: Which noun in 'The class showed honesty' is collective, and which is abstract?
questions.explanation: 'class' names a group (collective), while 'honesty' is a quality we cannot touch (abstract).

questions.question: In 'Sara gave a bunch of flowers to her friend', select ALL the nouns.
questions.explanation: All four are nouns: Sara (proper), bunch (collective), flowers (concrete/common), and friend (common).

questions.question: Which word is the proper noun in 'Priya keeps her courage even in Mumbai'?
questions.explanation: 'Priya' names a specific person (proper). 'Mumbai' is also proper. 'courage' is abstract.

questions.question: In 'A flock of geese flew over the calm lake', identify the collective noun and a concrete noun.
questions.explanation: 'flock' names the group (collective) and 'lake' is a place we can see and touch (concrete).

questions.question: Which type of noun is 'Ireland'?
questions.explanation: 'Ireland' names a specific country, so it is a proper noun.

questions.question: Which type of noun is 'milk powder'?
questions.explanation: 'milk powder' names a substance/material we measure rather than count, so it is a material (uncountable) noun.

questions.question: A single noun can never belong to more than one category (for example, both common and concrete).
questions.explanation: A noun can belong to more than one category at once — 'library', for example, is both a common noun and a concrete noun.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a proper noun, a collective noun, AND an abstract noun?
options: The Indian team played with great pride.
The dog ran in the park.
questions.explanation: 'Indian' (proper), 'team' (collective), and 'pride' (abstract) all appear in the first sentence.

questions.question: What are the indefinite articles?
questions.explanation: 'a' and 'an' are the indefinite articles, used for non-specific, general things.

questions.question: Which article is used before a word beginning with a vowel SOUND?
questions.explanation: 'an' is used before a vowel sound, like 'an apple' or 'an owl'.

questions.question: Which article is used before a word beginning with a consonant SOUND?
questions.explanation: 'a' is used before a consonant sound, like 'a book' or 'a tree'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'She wants to become ____ astronaut.'
questions.explanation: 'astronaut' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an astronaut'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'I saw ____ owl in the garden.'
questions.explanation: 'owl' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an owl'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'I saw ____ one-eyed cat.'
questions.explanation: Even though 'one' is spelled with a vowel, it begins with a 'w' consonant sound (‘won’), so we use 'a one-eyed cat'.

questions.question: Which article correctly completes 'She found ____ old coin.'?
questions.explanation: 'old' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an old coin'.

questions.question: We use 'an' before words that begin with a vowel sound.
questions.explanation: 'an' is used before vowel sounds, like 'an egg' or 'an hour'.

questions.question: Which is correct?
questions.explanation: The 'h' in 'hour' is silent, so it begins with a vowel sound — we use 'an hour'.

questions.question: Which is correct?
questions.explanation: 'university' begins with a 'yoo' consonant sound, so we use 'a university', not 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'He read ____ interesting book.'
questions.explanation: 'interesting' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an interesting book'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'She has ____ pet dog.'
questions.explanation: 'pet' begins with a consonant sound and this is the first mention, so we use 'a pet dog'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'I watched ____ amazing video about space.'
questions.explanation: 'amazing' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an amazing video'.

questions.question: We use 'a' before words that begin with a consonant sound.
questions.explanation: 'a' is used before consonant sounds, like 'a cat' or 'a house'.

questions.question: Why do we say 'an honest man' but 'a happy man'?
options: 'honest' has a silent 'h' (vowel sound); 'happy' has a spoken 'h' (consonant sound)
'honest' is a special word with no rule
There is no difference; both should use 'a'
questions.explanation: The 'h' in 'honest' is silent, so it sounds like a vowel ('onest') and takes 'an'. The 'h' in 'happy' is spoken, so it takes 'a'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the indefinite article correctly?
questions.explanation: 'apple' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an apple' is correct.

questions.question: Which article completes 'It takes ____ hour to finish.' correctly?
questions.explanation: 'hour' has a silent 'h' and begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an hour'.

questions.question: Select ALL the phrases that correctly use 'an'.
questions.explanation: 'an elephant' and 'an idea' begin with vowel sounds. 'dog' and 'book' begin with consonant sounds, so they take 'a'.

questions.question: The indefinite articles 'a' and 'an' are used with ____ nouns.
questions.explanation: 'a' and 'an' are used with singular, non-specific (general) countable nouns.

questions.question: Which sentence is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: 'owl' begins with a vowel sound, so it should be 'an owl', not 'a owl'.

questions.question: What is the definite article?
questions.explanation: 'the' is the definite article, used for specific things that are already known.

questions.question: When do we use 'the'?
options: When talking about a specific thing already known
questions.explanation: 'the' is used when we refer to a specific object or noun that is already known to the reader or listener.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'She has a pet dog and ____ dog loves to play.'
questions.explanation: 'the' is used for the second mention because we are now talking about the same, specific dog.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'I saw an owl sitting on ____ tree, then the owl flew to ____ same tree again.'
questions.explanation: The tree is mentioned generally first ('a tree'), then referred to again specifically ('the same tree').

questions.question: We use 'the' when we mention something for the second time because it is now specific.
questions.explanation: The first mention is general ('a dog'), but the second mention is specific and known, so we use 'the dog'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: '____ mangoes in this basket are fresh and juicy.'
questions.explanation: We use 'The' because we are pointing to specific mangoes — the ones in this particular basket.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'the' for something unique?
options: The sun rises in the east.
A sun rises in an east.
An sun rises in a east.
x sun rises in x east.
questions.explanation: We use 'the' for unique things like the sun and directions like the east, so 'The sun rises in the east' is correct.

questions.question: Which article do we use before the names of rivers, seas, and oceans?
questions.explanation: We use 'the' before names of rivers, seas, and oceans, like 'the Ganga' or 'the Pacific Ocean'.

questions.question: Select ALL the phrases where 'the' is used correctly.
questions.explanation: 'the moon' (unique) and 'the Himalayas' (mountain range) correctly use 'the'. The others are incorrect.

questions.question: In 'He's crawling out of the duckweed', why is 'the' used before 'duckweed'?
options: It refers to the specific duckweed in the pond already being talked about
questions.explanation: 'the' points to the specific duckweed in the pond that the poem is describing, so it is definite.

questions.question: We use 'the' before the names of specific mountain ranges, like 'the Alps'.
questions.explanation: 'the' is used before names of mountain ranges (the Alps, the Himalayas) and groups of islands.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'the' correctly for a specific object?
options: Please close the door behind you.
Please close a door I have never seen.
questions.explanation: 'the door' refers to a specific, known door, so 'the' is correct.

questions.question: What is the 'zero article'?
options: Using no article at all before certain nouns
Using a capital letter instead of an article
questions.explanation: The zero article means we use no article (shown as 'x') before certain nouns.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'We had ____ dinner at 8 o'clock.'
questions.explanation: We use no article (x) before meal names like dinner, lunch, and breakfast.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'He plays ____ football with his friends.'
questions.explanation: We use no article (x) before the names of games and sports like football.

questions.question: We do not use an article before the names of games and sports.
questions.explanation: Games and sports like football, cricket, and chess take the zero article (no article).

questions.question: Select ALL the nouns that usually take NO article (zero article).
questions.explanation: Games (football) and languages (Japanese) take the zero article. 'apple' takes 'an' and 'moon' takes 'the'.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: 'School starts at ____ 8 a.m.'
questions.explanation: We use no article (x) before hours, days, and months, so 'at 8 a.m.' takes the zero article.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the zero article?
options: People speak the Japanese in the Japan.
People speak a Japanese in an Japan.
People speak an Japanese in the Japan.
questions.explanation: Languages (Japanese) and countries like Japan take no article, so 'People speak Japanese in Japan' is correct.

questions.question: We use no article before uncountable nouns like 'butter' when speaking generally.
questions.explanation: Uncountable nouns used generally take the zero article, as in 'I love x butter'.

questions.question: Which sentence uses articles CORRECTLY?
options: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
The Tokyo is a capital of the Japan.
A Tokyo is the capital of an Japan.
An Tokyo is a capital of Japan.
questions.explanation: Cities (Tokyo) and countries (Japan) take no article, but 'the capital' is specific, so 'Tokyo is the capital of Japan' is correct.

questions.question: Which noun below takes the zero article when used generally?
questions.explanation: 'custard' is uncountable and takes no article when general ('I want to eat x custard'). Owl takes 'an', hour takes 'an', moon takes 'the'.

questions.question: Select ALL the sentences that correctly use the zero article.
options: I saw the owl on a tree.
questions.explanation: Days (Fridays) and games (cricket) take no article. The other two correctly use 'the' and 'an', not zero article.

questions.question: Before which of these do we usually use NO article?
options: singular countable nouns mentioned for the first time
questions.explanation: Languages like English, Hindi, and Japanese take the zero article (no article).

questions.question: Who wrote the poem 'Daddy Fell into the Pond'?
questions.explanation: The poem 'Daddy Fell into the Pond' was written by Alfred Noyes.

questions.question: What was the weather like at the beginning of the poem?
questions.explanation: The poem begins 'Everyone grumbled. The sky was grey.' — the weather was dull and gloomy.

questions.question: How did everyone feel at the start of the poem?
questions.explanation: Everyone grumbled and had 'nothing to do and nothing to say' — they felt bored and gloomy.

questions.question: What sudden event changed the mood of the poem?
questions.explanation: The dull mood suddenly changed when 'Daddy fell into the pond!' and everyone became merry.

questions.question: What did Timothy do after Daddy fell into the pond?
questions.explanation: The poem says 'And Timothy danced for sheer delight' — he danced with joy.

questions.question: Why did someone ask for the camera?
options: To take a picture of Daddy climbing out of the pond
questions.explanation: Someone shouted 'Give me the camera, quick, oh quick!' to photograph Daddy crawling out of the duckweed.

questions.question: How did the family's faces change after Daddy fell in?
questions.explanation: The poem says 'And everyone's face grew merry and bright' — everyone became cheerful.

questions.question: What did the gardener do when Daddy fell into the pond?
options: Slapped his knee and shook with silent laughter
questions.explanation: 'Then the gardener suddenly slapped his knee, And doubled up, shaking silently' — he laughed silently.

questions.question: How did the ducks react in the poem?
options: They quacked as if they were daft
questions.explanation: 'And the ducks all quacked as if they were daft' — they quacked as though they were being silly.

questions.question: In the poem, Daddy falling into the pond made everyone happy.
questions.explanation: The unexpected fall turned the dull day joyful — everyone's face grew merry and bright.

questions.question: What is the main message of the poem?
options: Unexpected moments can bring joy to a dull day
We should never laugh at others
questions.explanation: The poem shows that even a boring, gloomy day can suddenly turn happy because of an unexpected event.

questions.question: What does the line 'there wasn't a thing that didn't respond' suggest?
options: Everyone and everything reacted to the funny moment
questions.explanation: It means every person and even the animals reacted to the funny event — the whole scene came alive with laughter.

questions.question: What was covering Daddy as he crawled out of the pond?
questions.explanation: The poem describes him 'crawling out of the duckweed' — the tiny floating plants covered him.

questions.question: The poem shows that even animals like the ducks and drake seemed to join in the fun.
questions.explanation: The ducks quacked 'as if they were daft' and 'it sounded as if the old drake laughed' — even the animals seemed to respond.

questions.question: How does the poet mostly make the poem funny?
options: By describing a surprising, silly situation and everyone's reactions
By making the reader feel sad
questions.explanation: The humour comes from the surprising, silly situation of Daddy falling in and the lively, exaggerated reactions of everyone around.

questions.question: What sound word in the poem shows the camera taking a photo?
questions.explanation: The single word 'Click!' shows the moment the camera took the photo of Daddy.

questions.question: What does the word 'grumble' mean?
options: To complain in a bad-tempered way
questions.explanation: 'grumble' means to complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

questions.question: What does the word 'dismal' mean?
options: Causing a mood of gloom or sadness
questions.explanation: 'dismal' means causing a mood of gloom or depression — a dull, gloomy day.

questions.question: What does the word 'duckweed' mean?
options: A tiny aquatic plant that floats on still water
questions.explanation: 'duckweed' is a tiny aquatic flowering plant that floats in large quantities on still water.

questions.question: What does the word 'daft' mean?
questions.explanation: 'daft' means silly or foolish.

questions.question: What is a 'drake'?
questions.explanation: A 'drake' is a male duck.

questions.question: In 'Timothy danced for sheer delight', what does 'sheer' mean?
questions.explanation: 'sheer' here means 'nothing other than' — his delight was complete and pure.

questions.question: 'Dismal' means the same as cheerful and bright.
questions.explanation: 'dismal' means gloomy and depressing — the opposite of cheerful and bright.

questions.question: Which word is the OPPOSITE (antonym) of 'grumble'?
questions.explanation: 'grumble' means to complain, so its opposite is 'praise'. The other options are similar to grumble.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'daft' correctly?
options: The ducks quacked in a daft, silly way.
She solved the daft, difficult sum quickly.
questions.explanation: 'daft' means silly or foolish, so 'a daft, silly way' uses it correctly.

questions.question: A 'dismal day' is best described as a day that is ____.
questions.explanation: 'dismal' means gloomy, so a dismal day is a gloomy and dull one.

questions.question: 'Duckweed' floats on the surface of still water.
questions.explanation: Duckweed is a tiny aquatic plant that floats in large quantities on still water.

questions.question: Which word from the poem could replace 'foolish' in a sentence?
questions.explanation: 'daft' means silly or foolish, so it could replace 'foolish'.

questions.question: What is alliteration?
options: The repeating of the same beginning sound in nearby words
A word that imitates a sound
questions.explanation: Alliteration is when words close together begin with the same sound, like 'Peter's piglet paddled in purple puddles'.

questions.question: Which sentence is an example of alliteration?
options: Peter's piglet paddled in purple puddles.
questions.explanation: 'Peter's piglet paddled in purple puddles' repeats the 'p' sound, making it alliteration.

questions.question: What is a hyperbole?
options: An exaggeration that is not meant to be taken seriously
questions.explanation: A hyperbole is a way of writing that exaggerates to make something sound more exciting, like 'My backpack weighs a ton'.

questions.question: Which sentence is a hyperbole?
options: I told you a million times to clean your room!
The sun is very bright today.
He drinks water when he's thirsty.
questions.explanation: 'I told you a million times' is a huge exaggeration, so it is a hyperbole.

questions.question: Select ALL the sentences that are hyperboles (exaggerations).
options: It was so cold, even the polar bears were shivering.
That joke was so funny, I laughed my head off!
The sun is very bright today.
He drinks water when he's thirsty.
questions.explanation: The first two are exaggerations not meant literally, so they are hyperboles. The last two are ordinary, factual sentences.

questions.question: Alliteration uses the same beginning sound in words that are close together.
questions.explanation: Alliteration repeats the same starting sound in nearby words, like 'silly snakes slither slowly'.

questions.question: 'He ran faster than the wind.' Which figure of speech is this?
questions.explanation: Running 'faster than the wind' is an exaggeration for effect, so it is a hyperbole.

questions.question: Which of these best shows alliteration?
questions.explanation: 'Big brown bears bounce' repeats the 'b' sound at the start of each word, making it alliteration.

questions.question: The sentence 'I'm so hungry I could eat a horse' is a hyperbole.
questions.explanation: It is a big exaggeration — you can't really eat a horse — so it is a hyperbole.

questions.question: Why do writers use hyperbole?
options: To make something sound more exciting or dramatic
To make a boring, factual list
questions.explanation: Hyperbole exaggerates to make writing sound more exciting, funny, or dramatic — it is not meant literally.

questions.question: Which noun would need a capital letter if it started a name?
questions.explanation: When 'river' is part of a specific name like 'River Ganga', it becomes a proper noun and takes a capital letter.

questions.question: Which is a proper noun in 'We celebrated Diwali with our family'?
questions.explanation: 'Diwali' is the name of a specific festival, so it is a proper noun. 'family' is a collective noun.

questions.question: The word 'boy' can be a proper noun.
questions.explanation: 'boy' is a general name for a person, so it is a common noun, not a proper noun.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a countable noun correctly in the plural?
options: There are five books on the shelf.
questions.explanation: 'books' is countable and correctly plural. Furniture, water, and sugar are uncountable and have no plural form.

questions.question: Which measuring phrase is correct for an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: Bread is uncountable, so we measure it with 'a loaf of bread'.

questions.question: Select ALL the correct collective-noun phrases.
questions.explanation: 'a pack of wolves' and 'a flock of birds' are correct. Ships take 'fleet' and bees take 'swarm', so the other two are wrong.

questions.question: Which word changes an action into an abstract noun: 'to be free' becomes ____?
questions.explanation: 'freedom' is the abstract noun form — it names the idea of being free.

questions.question: Which sentence has an abstract noun as its subject?
questions.explanation: 'Honesty' is a quality we cannot touch, so it is an abstract noun, and here it is the subject of the sentence.

questions.question: In 'The choir sang with great emotion in London', name the collective, abstract, and proper nouns.
options: choir = collective; emotion = abstract; London = proper
choir = abstract; emotion = proper; London = collective
choir = proper; emotion = collective; London = abstract
questions.explanation: 'choir' names a group (collective), 'emotion' is a feeling (abstract), and 'London' names a specific city (proper).

questions.question: Which noun is uncountable in 'She poured milk into a cup'?
questions.explanation: 'milk' is uncountable (we measure it), while 'cup' is a countable noun.

questions.question: In 'a bunch of keys', 'bunch' is a collective noun and 'keys' is a countable concrete noun.
questions.explanation: 'bunch' names the group (collective), and 'keys' can be counted and touched (countable concrete).

questions.question: Which article completes 'He is ____ honest boy.' correctly?
questions.explanation: 'honest' has a silent 'h' and begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an honest boy'.

questions.question: Which article completes 'I need ____ umbrella.' correctly?
questions.explanation: 'umbrella' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an umbrella'.

questions.question: Which phrase is correct?
options: x European country as a rule
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with a 'yoo' consonant sound, so we use 'a European country', not 'an'.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'the' for a musical instrument?
options: She plays a violin that no one knows.
She plays x violin as a rule.
questions.explanation: We use 'the' before the names of musical instruments, so 'She plays the violin' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the article: 'Have you seen ____ Eiffel Tower in Paris?'
questions.explanation: 'the' is used before the names of famous, unique monuments like the Eiffel Tower.

questions.question: Choose the article: 'I go to school by ____ bus.' (general way of travel)
questions.explanation: In fixed travel phrases like 'by bus', 'by car', or 'by train', we use no article.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the zero article before a meal?
options: We had the breakfast at seven.
We had a breakfast at seven always.
We had an breakfast at seven.
questions.explanation: Meal names like breakfast, lunch, and dinner usually take no article, so 'We had breakfast' is correct.

questions.question: Select ALL the sentences that use articles correctly.
questions.explanation: Languages (Hindi, English) and games (chess) take no article. 'an best' and 'a elephant' are wrong ('the best' and 'an elephant').

questions.question: Which sentence uses BOTH 'a' and 'an' correctly?
options: I bought a pen and an eraser.
I bought an pen and a eraser.
I bought a pen and a eraser.
I bought an pen and an eraser.
questions.explanation: 'pen' has a consonant sound (a pen) and 'eraser' has a vowel sound (an eraser), so 'a pen and an eraser' is correct.

questions.question: In 'The children played in the park', why is 'the' used before 'children'?
options: It refers to specific, known children
questions.explanation: 'the children' refers to specific children already known to the reader, so 'the' is used.

questions.question: The choice between 'a' and 'an' depends on the SOUND at the start of the next word, not just the letter.
questions.explanation: We choose 'a' or 'an' by the sound: 'an hour' (vowel sound) but 'a university' (consonant sound), even though the letters differ.

questions.question: Which sentence has two proper nouns?
questions.explanation: 'Ravi' (person) and 'Delhi' (place) are both proper nouns, so the first sentence has two.

questions.question: Which pair shows a concrete noun and its related abstract noun?
questions.explanation: 'friend' is concrete (a person you can see) and 'friendship' is abstract (the feeling/idea), so they are a related pair.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a collective noun correctly?
options: A team of doctors treated the patients.
A team of a doctor treated them.
A herd of doctors treated them.
questions.explanation: 'A team of doctors' correctly uses the collective noun 'team' for a group of doctors.

questions.question: In 'The Indian army showed great bravery', which word is abstract?
questions.explanation: 'bravery' is a quality we cannot touch (abstract). 'army' is collective and 'Indian' is proper.

questions.question: Which of these nouns is uncountable?
questions.explanation: 'rice' is uncountable — we measure it rather than count each grain. The others are countable.

questions.question: What lesson can we learn from the reactions in the poem?
options: A little laughter can brighten even a gloomy day
We should never play near ponds
questions.explanation: The poem shows how one funny moment turned a dull, gloomy day into a joyful one — laughter can brighten our mood.

questions.question: At the start of the poem, the family had ____.
options: nothing to do and nothing to say
questions.explanation: The poem says 'We had nothing to do and nothing to say' — the family was bored.

questions.question: The repeated line 'Daddy fell into the pond!' helps show how important that moment was to the poem.
questions.explanation: The line is repeated to highlight the key event that changed the whole mood of the day.

questions.question: Which word best fits: 'The old ____, a male duck, floated on the pond.'
questions.explanation: A 'drake' is a male duck, so it fits the sentence best.

questions.question: Which word means 'to complain in a bad-tempered way'?
questions.explanation: 'grumble' means to complain in a bad-tempered way.

questions.question: Repeating the same first sound in nearby words, like 'silly snakes slither', is called ____.
questions.explanation: Repeating the same beginning sound in nearby words is called alliteration.

questions.question: 'My bag weighs a ton!' What does this hyperbole really mean?
options: The bag weighs exactly one ton
The bag is made of metal
questions.explanation: It is an exaggeration meaning the bag feels very heavy — not that it literally weighs a ton.

questions.question: A hyperbole should be taken as an exact, literal fact.
questions.explanation: A hyperbole is a deliberate exaggeration and is not meant to be taken literally.
